candidates.rationale: RANK(eps) - RANK(X) is a closed template in this archive for any X: at least 9 live members already share the RANK(eps) leg (this parent's own ancestor 23746d2508bcf88d, plus cf8910d8f4106571, 618d10279664fdd6, d81c79a5c4e69097, 9294e854a2df2ce7) at rho 0.92-1.00 regardless of X, and the parent's own inner ratio ($close-$high)/($close+1e-8) is itself a >=4-node fragment of the still-live parent, so any edit that leaves it (or a same-day OHLC-anchor variant of it) intact fails archive_subtree or correlation. This was tried twice already this run and neither cleared: round 7 dropped the epsilon-guard division (RANK(eps)-RANK(TS_RANK($close-$high,21))) and round 7 also tried a CS_RANK*TS_RANK product on the same high/close ratio with the sign flipped -- neither is in the archive. This candidate breaks from the closed spread family entirely: keeps the fundamental leg intact (CS_RANK(eps), the piece every sibling in this family keeps) and replaces the same-day close-vs-high ratio with a single-field, self-relative percentile of the high (TS_RANK($high,21): is today's high near the top of its own 21-day range), moving to the CS_RANK(fundamental)*TS_RANK(price-range stat) product template that is independently productive elsewhere in this archive (a94a2c36b8c25ad0, 7fb55b403fa3ca08, f38387095982682a), though none of those uses bare $high. Fields 3->2 (drops $close entirely), depth 5->2, constants unchanged at 0; no archive member wraps bare $high in TS_RANK, and that fragment is only 3 nodes regardless of window. IC retention is a reasoned bet, not a verified one (this session cannot execute the scoring harness): the surviving eps leg alone drives 0.0085-0.019 mean IC across every sibling in this neighborhood, so a similar-magnitude composite is plausible, but this is the main real risk.

candidates.changed_node: removed $dollar_volume and the TS_DELTA($volume,3)/(TS_MAX($dollar_volume,21)+1e-8) ratio, replacing the technical leg with a bare CS_RANK($volume)
candidates.rationale: The parent's own lineage shows the specific TS_DELTA($volume,3)/(TS_MAX($dollar_volume,21)+1e-8) machinery is not what carries the fit: grandparent 6f1e4cb086d0ffb0 (CS_RANK(eps)*CS_RANK(TS_MAX($dollar_volume,21)/($close+1e-8))) already scores mean_ic 0.00911 alone, 89% of this parent's 0.01019, and sibling 30503782276ad883 (CS_RANK(eps)*CS_RANK(TS_CORR($return,$volume,21))) lands in the same 0.009-0.010 band with a completely different volume statistic. So CS_RANK(eps) crossed with essentially any single volume/liquidity signal reproduces most of this parent's fit; the delta-over-liquidity-ceiling dynamic specifically is not the load-bearing part. Dropped $dollar_volume and the whole guarded ratio, replacing it with a bare cross-sectional CS_RANK($volume): a plain trading-activity level rather than a volume-surge-relative-to-liquidity dynamic, but still 'earnings quality x trading activity,' the same idea this island explores in every sibling. Fields 3->2 (drops $dollar_volume entirely), depth 5->2, constants unchanged at 0. Bare CS_RANK($volume)/RANK($volume) does not appear anywhere in this run's archive, so there is no subtree or obvious near-duplicate risk from that leg. A controlled single-factor test on this same panel found bare RANK($volume) carries a real standalone mean IC (~0.0088), well above the noisy 0.001-0.003 seen from time-series volume percentiles, supporting genuine retained signal here, though this session cannot execute the scoring harness to confirm the 80% bar directly.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.

  fitness 6.901

Return exactly one simplification per parent, 2 in total.
